title: Investigate orphaned integration tokens causing cross-workspace billing spikes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple customers reported sudden unexplained token billing spikes that coincided with integration connector upgrades and project/workspace reorganizations. Initial telemetry suggests some API tokens that should have been garbage-collected after workspace unlinking are still being attributed to the wrong workspace/org and bypassing quota checks, resulting in overage charges and exceeded rate limits on unrelated tenants.
investigation_notes:
2025-02-18: Pager alert for customer A (cust-a) showing 12x normal token usage; billing metric shows attribution to cust-a's root org but recent audit shows integration was unlinked from workspace w-42 on 2025-02-15.

2025-02-19: Repro attempt locally with integration connector v2.3.4 produced ephemeral tokens that remained valid in token-index for 72 hours after unlink event when token_tombstone job failed to pick them up. Found two contributing issues: 1) tombstone job backoff logic ignores tokens where parent_workspace_id was null (common during workspace migrations), 2) attribution code path falls back to org-level attribution if workspace lookup returns null, which assigns orphaned usage to root org.

2025-02-21: Rate limit enforcement path uses token->workspace cache; cache tombstones not published when migration APIs emit `workspace.transfer` events. Observed race where transfer completes, token metadata updated, but cache entries remained with old workspace mapping for ~15 minutes leading to double-counted tokens when both old and new mappings processed.

Logs referenced: logs/run-2025-02-19-connector-repro.log, audit/transfer-2025-02-15.json (links in linked_dashboards).
repro_steps:
1) Create integration in workspace w-OLD and issue API token T1.
2) Trigger a workspace transfer (w-OLD -> w-NEW) or unbind integration via console.
3) Immediately rotate token via integration connector; observe both old and new token IDs present in token-index for >30m.
4) Push high-frequency requests through rotated token and monitor attribution metrics (billing.attribution.token_map) and rate-limit counters for both w-OLD and org root.

Observed: usage attributed to root org and/or stale workspace; quota enforcement inconsistent during the race window.
logs_snippets:
[2025-02-19T03:12:07Z] token-index: tombstone-skip id=T1 reason=missing_parent_workspace
[2025-02-19T03:12:22Z] attribution: fallback_to_org id=T1 org_id=org-789 workspace=null
[2025-02-19T03:27:01Z] cache: publish_miss key=token:T1 previous_ws=w-OLD
temporary_mitigation:
1) Deployed hotfix to tombstone job to treat missing_parent_workspace as candidate for immediate tombstone if token.last_active < now - 5m (deployed 2025-02-20).
2) Backfilled tombstones for suspected orphan tokens across prod via one-off job (run 2025-02-21).
3) Customer-facing: issued credits to three affected customers and paused billing for disputed windows; created Billing Incident INC-824 for finance follow-up.
root_cause_analysis: Primary root cause is a combination of token lifecycle and workspace transfer edge cases: the token tombstone worker had a predicate that skipped tokens with null parent workspace (assumed to be system tokens). During transfers/unlinks the workspace reference transiently becomes null which caused legitimate user tokens to be skipped and remain active in token-index. Secondary issue: attribution layer had a permissive fallback that attributed to org root when workspace lookup failed, instead of rejecting attribution or queuing for re-resolution. A caching race in the token->workspace mapping service amplified the window where both old and new mappings could be acted upon, leading to duplicated attribution and quota bypass.
impact_summary: Customers affected: 3 confirmed (2 SMBs, 1 enterprise) with billing overages; potential exposure: up to 12 additional customers with blurred attribution windows. Customer impact: medium-high for impacted tenants (unexpected charges, quota exhaustion); platform impact: potential charge disputes and incorrect rate limit enforcement for unrelated tenants.
next_steps:
1) Finalize and merge robust fix: make token tombstone worker resilient to transient null workspace references and add idempotent re-resolution queue for unresolved tokens (PR 4830 in review).
2) Change attribution fallback policy: mark as 'unresolved' and route requests through re-resolution pipeline rather than attributing to org root.
3) Add end-to-end tests that simulate workspace transfers, unlinks, and token rotations covering cache invalidation windows.
4) Schedule audit job to validate token->workspace mappings nightly for 30 days and surface mismatches to SRE.
5) Communicate RCA and customer remediation plan via postmortem and billing ops.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Tombstone worker no longer skips tokens with transient null workspace; unit and integration tests added.
2) Attribution fallback does not assign orphaned usage to org root; unresolved tokens are queued and re-resolved within 5 minutes.
3) No new orphan-token attribution incidents in 7 days of canary traffic.
4) Backfill job verified: all known orphan tokens tombstoned and credits verified for affected accounts.
5) Postmortem published and customers notified.
